High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Rakesh Singh - Panel Lawyer for State.
Shri Vivek Shukla - Advocate for objector.
Heard on I.A. No.15897 of 2025 which is fourth application under Section 430(1) of BNSS, 2023 for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.
Earlier three applications for suspension of sentence and grant of bail were dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 12.01.2022, 07.03.2024 and 06.01.2025.

This Criminal Appeal assails the judgment dated 09.12.2019 passed by the learned Special Judge,
POCSO Act, Katni (M.P.) in Special Case No.2700044 of 2016, whereby the appellant has been convicted under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(n) and 506 (Part-II) of the IPC and sentence to undergo R.I. for 05 years and fine of Rs.2,000/-, R.I. for 10 years and fine of Rs.2,000/-, R.I. for 05 years and fine of Rs.2,000/- and R.I. for 03 years and fine of Rs.2,000/- respectively, with default stipulations.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the present appellant has been in custody for approximately 6 years and 4 months.

The maximum sentence awarded by the learned trial Court is 10 years, and thus, the appellant has already undergone more than 50% of the custodial sentence imposed upon him, though, under Section 376(2)(n) of the IPC there is a 2 CRA-2446-2020 provision of minimum sentence of 10 years.
It is also submitted that the statements of prosecutrix and her parents are full of contradictions and omissions.
They exaggerate the story of the prosecution.
The concerned doctor has found no external injury on the person of the prosecutrix at the time of medical examination.

As far as the age of the prosecutrix is concerned, the principal, who has brought the scholar register has admitted that there is no birth certificate on record and there is no cogent proof with regard to the age of the prosecutrix that she was 14 to 16 years at the time of offence.

The sample for DNA is defective as there was no seal found on the packet by the examiner It is also submitted that present appellant is a disabled person and the allegation as levelled against him are fictitious.
It is further submitted that the appellant is ready to comply with the conditions as may be imposed by this Court.

The present appeal will take considerable time for its disposal and,
looking to the period of custody, benefit of suspension of sentence may be granted and the appellant may be released on bail during pendency of this appeal.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned Panel Lawyer for the State as well as learned counsel for the objector have opposed the prayer made by the appellant on the ground that FSL report and DNA report are positive.

As far as the age of the prosecutrix is concerned, there are ample evidence on record, which was available and as per that evidence the prosecutrix found to be 14-16 years of age at the time of incident, and therefore, no question of consent arises.
The ossification test also establishes the age of prosecutrix was between 14-16 years.

It is further submitted that keeping in view the 3 CRA-2446-2020 statements of the prosecutrix and her parents the charges levelled against the present appellants are found to be satisfactorily proved and beyond doubt, therefore, the learned trial Court was right in convicting and appropriately sentencing the appellant.
It is further submitted that there were 18 criminal cases registered against the present appellant.
In view of the aforesaid, no case for suspension of sentence and grant of bail is made out.
Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the record.

Although the appellant has already undergone custody for a period of six years and four months, but having regard to the fact that there is minimum sentence prescribed under Section 376(2)(n) of the IPC is ten years, and also in light of the ample material available on record against the appellant with respect to the charges,
as well as taking into consideration the criminal antecedents of the appellant, this Court without commenting upon the merits of the case, is not inclined to grant the benefit of suspension of sentence at this stage.
Accordingly, I.A. No.15897 of 2025 is hereby rejected.
(RAJENDRA KUMAR VANI) JUDGE THK Suraj Alias Buddhu Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148686492/
